content: Usually, man considers only the stubble field of transitoriness and overlooks the full granaries of the past, wherein he has salvaged once and for all his deeds, his joys, and also his sufferings.
author: Viktor Frankl
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

In Viktor Frankl's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
